metadata.title: Research
metadata.description: Adaptive physical intelligence for dexterous manipulation across scales: sensing, transferable learning, shared autonomy and embodiment, studied through tactile robotics, medical robotics and optical and magnetic microrobotics.

data.title: Optical Micromanipulation
data.description: We use optical tweezers to manipulate microscopic objects and fabricated microrobots. Our work combines optical-force modelling, microscopy-based perception and human–robot interaction to study controlled manipulation at small scales.
project: Platforms: Multi-spot optical tweezers, fabricated microrobots and interactive simulation.
Perception: Pose and depth estimation from microscopy, including physics-informed learning and sim-to-real data generation.
Control: Learning-based manipulation, digital-twin modelling and virtual visuo-haptic teleoperation.
Application focus: Precise handling of microscopic objects for biomedical research.
Recent work: ICRA 2026 sim-to-real perception; Du-FreqNet preprint; virtual visuo-haptic teleoperation preprint.

data.title: Magnetic Micromanipulation
data.description: We investigate how external magnetic fields can actuate and steer miniature robots. Our research connects actuation design, coordinated manipulation and adaptive shared control for navigation and interaction in constrained environments.
project: Platforms: Electromagnetic coils, permanent magnets and robot-assisted magnetic actuation.
Embodiment: Magnetic functionalisation, robot fabrication and reconfigurable actuation systems.
Control: Bimanual coordination, haptic guidance and learning from visual and language instructions.
Application focus: Microscale transport and biomedical manipulation research.
Recent work: magnetic microrobot fabrication; DexterousMag preprint; Mag-VLA preprint.

data.title: Robot-Assisted Microsurgery and Micromanipulation
data.description: We develop perception and control methods for precise manipulation with externally actuated tools, including micromanipulators and microsurgical robots. We study how visual feedback, motion scaling and shared autonomy can support reliable operation.
project: Platforms: Precision micromanipulators, piezoelectric positioning stages and robot-assisted microsurgery systems.
Perception: Multi-pipette localisation and image-based state estimation for patch-clamp workflows.
Interaction: Digital-twin teleoperation, adaptive motion scaling and human–robot shared control.
Application focus: Patch-clamp research, microsurgical training and delicate biological manipulation.
Recent work: multi-pipette localisation (IROS 2025); micro-dexterity review preprint.

vision.headline: Adaptive physical intelligence for dexterous manipulation across scales
vision.lead: We investigate how sensing, learning, control and robot design can work together to make dexterous manipulation adaptable to changing tasks and physical conditions.
vision.question: How can sensing, learning, control and embodiment be coupled to make dexterous manipulation adaptive?
vision.statement: Our goal is to develop robots that perceive physical interactions, adapt their behaviour and assist people in precise manipulation. We connect learning algorithms with the mechanics of sensors, tools and actuators, and evaluate these ideas through contact-rich tasks, medical robotics and scientific instrumentation.
vision.directionNote: Our four research themes connect tactile manipulation, human–robot shared control, and optical and magnetic microrobotics. Results from these platforms guide the next questions we investigate.

themes.title: Sensing and physical-state inference
themes.question: What can robots infer from touch and images?
themes.description: We combine tactile sensor design, multimodal learning and microscopy-based perception to estimate contact, material properties and object state. Our studies connect visual–tactile fusion and sensor-side computation with cross-sensor benchmarking and data-efficient pose and depth estimation.

evidence.name: ViTacTip
evidence.summary: A compact sensor combining visual, proximity and tactile information, with cross-modality interpretation and systematic benchmarking.

evidence.name: TacVerse
evidence.summary: A multisensor tactile dataset and benchmark that measures sensor shift, representation learning and few-shot adaptation.

evidence.name: Small-data micro-object pose estimation
evidence.summary: Simulation, image translation and feature learning support pose estimation from limited experimental microscopy data.

themes.nextStep: Extend physical-state estimation to changing sensors and contact conditions, with clearer estimates of uncertainty.

themes.title: Transferable and data-efficient skill learning
themes.question: How can skills transfer with limited new data?
themes.description: We develop learning methods that use structure in tasks, sensing and robot interaction to improve adaptation. Examples include one-shot imitation learning for pouring, multimodal diffusion policies for coordinated manipulation, and tactile skills transferred from simulation to physical robots.

evidence.name: One-shot domain-adaptive imitation learning
evidence.venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
evidence.summary: Progressive learning transfers a pouring skill to changed scenes and objects using limited new demonstration data.

evidence.name: ADM-DP
evidence.summary: A diffusion policy adaptively combines visual, tactile and spatial information for coordinated multi-agent manipulation.

evidence.name: Bi-Touch
evidence.summary: A collaborative study of bimanual tactile skills learned in simulation and transferred to physical robot arms.

themes.nextStep: Improve adaptation across tasks and embodiments while measuring the real data and interaction needed for transfer.

themes.title: Adaptive control and shared autonomy
themes.question: How should assistance adapt to the task and operator?
themes.description: We study how robots and people can share control during precise manipulation. Context-aware assistance, adaptive motion scaling, digital twins and haptic feedback connect human intent with the physical demands of a task. We evaluate these methods in robotic surgery, teleoperation and magnetic micromanipulation.

evidence.name: Context-aware surgical shared control
evidence.summary: Simulator-learned motions and context-dependent assistance are evaluated in user studies on a surgical research robot.

evidence.name: Digital twins with haptic teleoperation
evidence.summary: Mixed-reality teleoperation combines kinaesthetic and wearable tactile feedback, with user studies of the interface.

evidence.name: Adaptive microsurgical motion scaling
evidence.summary: Offline reinforcement learning and damping control adapt motion scaling for robot-assisted microsurgery research.

themes.nextStep: Develop assistance that responds to task uncertainty and changing interaction, with explicit evaluation of operator workload and physical performance.

themes.title: Embodiment and actuation design
themes.question: How does physical design shape capability?
themes.description: We investigate how materials, sensor geometry and actuation determine what a robot can sense and do. Our work includes inverse design of tactile elastomers, integrated tactile grippers, distributed optical-force control and modular magnetic robots. Physical design and control are developed together to enable new forms of manipulation.

evidence.name: i-Tac
evidence.summary: Inverse design links target optical and mechanical properties to printable tactile-elastomer compositions.

evidence.name: Distributed optical-force control
evidence.summary: Microrobot geometry and distributed laser-force allocation enable multi-axis manipulation with planar optical tweezers.

evidence.name: Modular magnetic millirobots
evidence.summary: Magnetic modules demonstrate locomotion, assembly, shape changes and cargo manipulation at the millimetre scale.

themes.nextStep: Study how changes to morphology and actuation can complement learning and control for new manipulation demands.

nextDirections.title: Predictive models of physical interaction
nextDirections.description: We aim to connect perception with models that anticipate contact, deformation and the consequences of action, while identifying where their predictions remain uncertain.

nextDirections.title: Learning across sensors and embodiments
nextDirections.description: Future work will investigate how representations and skills can transfer between different sensor designs, robot bodies and tasks with limited additional data.

nextDirections.title: Robotic tools for scientific experiments
nextDirections.description: Building on precision manipulation and scientific instrumentation, we aim to make experimental workflows more reproducible and explore how robots can support informative measurements.

framework.title: Four coupled questions, one physical interaction
framework.alt: Sensing physical state, learning useful behaviours, adapting action and assistance, and designing physical capability all connect through physical interaction. Contact, motion and observation inform these coupled research questions.
framework.caption: An explanatory map of the research programme. Sensing, learning, control and physical design inform one another through interaction; this is a synthesis of the research themes, not a single completed general-purpose system.

evidence.title: Read the evidence in its experimental context
evidence.alt: A reading guide for research: identify the task and conditions, examine the comparison, inspect the measurements and outcomes, and consider the supported scope and next question.
evidence.caption: A guide to reading the linked papers. Experimental platforms, data, comparators and evaluation criteria vary by study; the figure proposes questions for the reader rather than claiming that every project uses the same protocol.
